title: NoiseSDF2NoiseSDF: Learning Clean Neural Fields from Noisy Supervision
claim: Pixel coordinates give correspondences between noisy samples, raw points do not, but coordinates in neural fields restore them.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, red crosses vs green correspondence arrows
description: Three side-by-side panels compare coordinate correspondences between two noisy samples of the same thing. (a) Two overlapping noisy photos of a cameraman, overlaid with a grid. A red curved arrow links the same grid cell in both images, ending at a green label, 'Pixel-to-Pixel Correspondence'. (b) Blue and orange 3D spheres, scattered around two dashed curves, stand for two noisy point clouds. Red arrows with red X marks show that points do not match. The label 'Point-to-Point NO Correspondence' is in red. (c) Two stacked cubes show noisy SDF contour slices, with a red arrow linking the same coordinate and the green label 'Coordinate-to-Coordinate Correspondence'. Green stands for success and red for failure. Captions '(a)', '(b)' and '(c)' sit under each panel.
caption: Comparison of coordinate correspondences: (a) Pixel coordinates represent correspondences between two noisy images of the same scene. In contrast, (b) point coordinates do not exhibit correspondences between two noisy point clouds of the same shape. (c) SDF coordinates establish correspondences between two noisy neural fields representing the same shape.
abstract: Reconstructing accurate implicit surface representations from point clouds remains a challenging task, particularly when data is captured using low-quality scanning devices. These point clouds often contain substantial noise, leading to inaccurate surface reconstructions. Inspired by the Noise2Noise paradigm for 2D images, we introduce NoiseSDF2NoiseSDF, a novel method designed to extend this concept to 3D neural fields. Our approach enables learning clean neural SDFs from noisy point clouds through noisy supervision by minimizing the MSE loss between noisy SDF representations, allowing the network to implicitly denoise and refine surface estimations. We evaluate the effectiveness of NoiseSDF2NoiseSDF on benchmarks, including the ShapeNet, ABC, Famous, and Real datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that our framework significantly improves surface reconstruction quality from noisy inputs.
